summary: Brief spike of 5xxs from API gateway after TLS session cache corruption on runtime pool
description:
Issue summary: AtlasAI reported a sudden elevated 5xx rate for their tenant starting 2026-03-12 08:42 UTC. Errors surfaced at the API gateway and traced to upstream runtime nodes returning 502/503. Initial symptoms looked like connection resets and short-lived runtime restarts. The burst lasted ~18 minutes and impacted ~12% of requests for the tenant.

Context: AtlasAI is on a dedicated pool. Customer noticed failures across streaming and short-sync generation routes. They reported partial success when retrying later.

Requested outcome: fast mitigation and a permanent fix to prevent recurrence and guidance for customer on retries/pinning if needed.
impact: Customer-facing: intermittent 5xx on production endpoints for AtlasAI (dedicated). Estimated ~12% request failure rate during window; increased latency and streaming disconnects for ~18 minutes. Potential revenue and SLA exposure.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send concurrent generation requests (mix of short-sync and streaming) to customer tenant endpoint (tenant=atlasai) in us-east-1.
2) Observe elevated 502/503 responses on ~1 out of 8 requests when runtime pool rotates TLS sessions.
3) Reproduce more easily by toggling runtime graceful shutdown on a small subset of nodes (simulated) while sending streaming starts.
Note: reproduction requires load and timed runtime lifecycle events; not reliably reproducible in staging without simulating expired TLS session cache state.
observed_logs: [2026-03-12T08:42:11Z] apigw tenant=atlasai path=/v1/generate status=502 upstream=connection_reset by=proxy-01
[2026-03-12T08:42:12Z] runtime-12 ERROR: handshake timeout while accepting TLS session from lb-07; pending sessions backlog=132
[2026-03-12T08:42:15Z] runtime-12 INFO: initiating graceful shutdown (SIGTERM) to apply kernel update
[2026-03-12T08:42:17Z] runtime-12 WARN: TLS session cache lookup failed: corrupted-entry id=0x7f8a3d
[2026-03-12T08:59:02Z] apigw tenant=atlasai status=200 request_id=... resumed normal traffic
investigation_notes: 03/12 09:05 - Support triage: Elevated 5xx coincident with a small wave of runtime graceful shutdowns in the dedicated pool. Hypothesis: outgoing TLS sessions and session-cache entries became inconsistent during in-flight handshakes, causing a short-term handshake/backlog that propagated to apigw as 502/503.
03/12 09:20 - Eng (runtime) reproduced in lab by creating stale session-cache entries and performing rapid graceful restarts; observed TLS handshake aborts and a backlog inside the accept queue.

03/12 09:35 - Observed that load-balancer retried to different runtime nodes which sometimes had orphaned cache handles leading to per-node memory pressure and transient worker OOMs on runtime-12; restart cascade lasted ~18 minutes while pool autoscaler drained and warmed new nodes.
03/12 10:00 - Correlation with LB healthcheck churn: nodes that failed healthchecks were cycled; combined with session-cache corruption this amplified the 5xx surface area.
03/12 11:10 - No evidence of tenant-specific request payload patterns; impact appears infrastructure lifecycle-related.
Hypothesis status: high confidence that TLS session cache corruption + overlapping graceful shutdowns caused transient handshake failures and increased upstream unavailability reports to apigw.
comments: Sofia Patel (support) 2026-03-12 09:10: Customer reported 12% error rate; forwarded initial logs and asked for urgent triage.

Marcus Chen (runtime eng) 2026-03-12 09:22: Started reproducer with stale session-cache + restart. I can reproduce handshake failures; capturing tcpdump and runtime debug logs now. Marking as P1 Sev1 and escalating to SRE for LB healthcheck tuning.

Elena Ruiz (SRE) 2026-03-12 09:34: Observed accept queue backlog on lb-07 and increased SYN_RECV; temporarily increased accept queue and extended healthcheck grace window to reduce churn. Monitoring for stabilization.

AtlasAI (customer) 2026-03-12 09:45: Thanks — we saw errors drop after you increased healthcheck grace. Please advise on long-term fix; this happened during a scheduled kernel patch on our dedicated pool.

Marcus Chen (runtime eng) 2026-03-12 10:05: Identified a bug in TLS session cache eviction where entries marked during shutdown weren't atomically cleared, leaving corrupt handles. Patch prepared (runtime PR linked). Will coordinate hotfix rollout during low traffic window.
Sofia Patel (support) 2026-03-12 11:08: Customer confirmed service returned to expected levels; keeping ticket open for patch rollout and postmortem.
resolution: Mitigation applied: SRE increased LB healthcheck grace and accept-queue; runtime team pushed a hotfix to atomically clear session-cache entries on shutdown (PR merged and small canary rollout completed in us-east-1). Post-rollout monitoring for 24h showed no recurrence. Root cause: race in TLS session cache eviction during graceful shutdowns leading to corrupted handles and handshake aborts.
workaround: If customers see similar errors during maintenance windows: 1) pause client retries briefly (5s) then retry; 2) request support to delay kernel/runtime restarts by 1-2 minutes while autoscaler warms nodes; 3) for dedicated tenants, schedule maintenance windows with Redwood Ops to minimize overlap.
next_steps: 1) Postmortem doc: create Confluence page with timeline and mitigation steps (assigned to Marcus).
2) Backport hotfix to stable runtime branches and schedule canaries in eu-west and us-west next maintenance window.
3) Add an automated check in deploy pipeline to prevent overlapping graceful shutdown waves across a single dedicated pool.
4) Follow up with AtlasAI CS to confirm SLA impact and any crediting required.
